title: Monotonicity under coordinate bribery
statement: Let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$ be nondecreasing in each coordinate, meaning that changing any one coordinate from $-1$ to $1$ cannot decrease its value. For every finite set of coordinates $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and every input $x$, the value of $f$ at $x$ is at most its value at the input obtained by setting every coordinate in $J$ to $1$ and leaving all other coordinates unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
$J$ is a finite set of coordinates
$x$ is an input in the sign cube
